stories.title: Kohat Police Lines attack mastermind killed in joint operation in KP's Lakki Marwat: CTD
stories.brief: The CTD said in a statement that the slain terrorist, whom the law enforcement department identified as Zahid Gul, was the mastermind of the attack on Kohat Police Lines.

stories.title: PM reaffirms Pakistan’s support for Saudi Arabia amid Houthi attacks in meeting with newly appointed envoy
stories.brief: The newly appointed Ambassador of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia to Pakistan, H.E. Significance of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement The MJDA was the latest step in longstanding military and strategic cooperation between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye.

stories.title: Stewart and Morris add to GB gold tally at Worlds
stories.brief: Mark Stewart and Anna Morris add to Great Britain's gold medal tally on day three of the Track Cycling World Championships in Shanghai.

stories.title: Morris wins omnium gold for Great Britain
stories.brief: Great Britain's Anna Morris wins gold in the women's omnium at the Track Cycling World Championships in Shanghai.

stories.title: Karachi court acquits alleged drug baroness Anmol alias Pinky in two more cases
stories.brief: KARACHI: A sessions court in Karachi on Friday acquitted alleged drug queenpin Anmol alias Pinky in two narcotics cases. She appeared before the South additional and sessions judge via a video link at the hearing of her applications today, and the court acquitted her, citing a lack of evidence in both cases.

stories.title: KP Governor Kundi announces amended welfare scheme for police officers, martyrs’ families
stories.brief: The provincial government has increased compensation for the families of martyred police officers and amended the previous plot allotment scheme, opting to pay the families cash in lieu of plots.

stories.title: GB's Stewart wins gold in thrilling points race
stories.brief: Great Britain's Mark Stewart wins gold after a thrilling end to the men's points race at the 2026 Track Cycling World Championships.

stories.title: 18 countries, including Pakistan, condemn inauguration of Colombian embassy in Jerusalem
stories.brief: Eighteen countries, including Pakistan, on Friday strongly condemned the opening of the Colombian embassy in Jerusalem, stating that any move to recognise the city as Israel’s capital had no legal effect.

stories.title: Karachi court acquits cocaine queen 'Pinky' in two drug cases
stories.brief: A district and sessions court in Karachi on Friday acquitted Anmol alias Pinky in two drug-related cases registered by the Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD) and Gizri police, citing a lack of evidence. Read: Karachi court acquits drug queenpin 'Pinky' in three cases A case was registered against Anmol at the CTD police station in 2018.

stories.title: K-P raises compensation for martyred police personnel to up to Rs35m
stories.brief: The families of martyred superintendents of police (SPs), senior superintendents of police (SSPs), assistant inspectors-general and officers in grades 18 and 19 would receive Rs30 million, compared with the previous Rs21 million.

stories.title: Pakistan, 18 countries reject Colombia’s Jerusalem embassy, says move has 'no legal effect'
stories.brief: Pakistan and 18 other countries have condemned Colombia’s inauguration of its embassy in Jerusalem, saying any move to recognise the city as Israel’s capital was “null and void” and had no legal effect, according to a Foreign Office (FO) statement issued on Friday.

stories.title: Watch: Did Tesla really just unveil a flying car?
stories.brief: Tesla CEO Elon Musk showcased the vehicle at a facility owned by his SpaceX company, which helped develop the model.

stories.title: Living with a stink? Technology might help
stories.brief: Smells from rubbish dumps and industrial facilities are being more carefully monitored.

stories.title: Tech market sell-off deepens amid fears over US inflation and AI debt
stories.brief: Chip makers and tech investors such as Samsung and SoftBank plunge as potential interest rate hikes spook marketsBusiness news – live updatesLarry Elliott: the global economy is muddling through.

stories.title: What does assuming the chairmanship of the IMF, World Bank governing boards mean for Pakistan?
stories.brief: Pakistan has been selected to chair the Boards of Governors of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and World Bank Group (WBG) in 2027, marking its return to the position after 74 years.

stories.title: Naqvi takes veiled swipe at political party chief over K-P governorship
stories.brief: Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi on Friday criticised a political party’s chief over his opposition to the imposition of governor’s rule in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa, saying the politician was “extremely angry” over not being given a role in the move or being offered the governorship.

stories.title: Families of children killed in Peshawar school roof collapse demand justice
stories.brief: The families of children killed in a roof collapse at a school in Peshawar called for "justice" on Friday, the day after more than 30 pupils and a teacher were crushed to death.

stories.title: Pakistan to assume IMF, World Bank board chairmanship for first time in over 7 decades
stories.brief: Pakistan has been named the incoming chair of the Boards of Governors of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank Group (WBG) for next year, for the first time since 1953, the Ministry of Economic Affairs said on Friday.

stories.title: Rogue AI agents broke into Indian firms' live systems, government says
stories.brief: AI models under test broke into Indian organisations' live systems and read confidential records undetected, India's ​cybersecurity agency said, the country's first such official ‌account after similar incidents of rogue AI behavior worldwide.

stories.title: Sanaullah links reversal of K-P governor's rule to PTI support for counterterrorism efforts
stories.brief: Speaking to a private news channel, Sanaullah said the government wanted all political parties to reach a consensus on counterterrorism, arguing that growing security challenges required a unified response from the federal and provincial governments.
